To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the transverse momentum spectrum of gluon jets close to the rapidty gap, in diffractive DIS, is peaked around a characteristic scale, and 2) that this characteristic scale can be used to study saturation.
in large-mass diffractions in DIS, the gluon jets close to the rapidty gap have a spectrum of transverse momenta peaked around a value that caracterizes the onset on S-matrix unitariety.
the diffractive gluon jet is characterized by a transverse momentum spectrum peaked around a value that is related to the onset of saturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: - the study of the gluon jet structure in diffractive events in deep inelastic electron-proton scattering, - the study of diffraction in deep-inelastic electron-proton collisions at high energies, - the study and the development of new techniques to measure diffractive events at HERA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the saturation picture is not in contradiction with the present data, but also that it is not yet proven.
the saturation model is not able to explain the HERA data.
, at the present energies and in the kinematical range of the HERA experiments, the gluon jet in large-mass diffration is a clear signature for the onset of unitarity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the saturation of the gluon density at high energies can lead to the saturation of the S-matrix at large rapidity gaps, and that the onset of the S-matter unitarity is a natural consequence of the saturation of the parton density.
in the present energies we do not see any sign of saturation, although we do not exclude that at the LHC energies, the onset of saturation will become visible in diffraction.
we have studied the gluon jet in diffractive deep inelastic scattering and have shown that it is peaked around a characteristic transverse momentum value which is related to the onset of unitarity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of diffractive processes in DIS is a promising way to test the saturation picture of the proton wavefunction.
a large rapidity gap is not sufficient to probe the saturation regime.
, at least for the kinematical region we are studying, the onset of unitarity is not a consequence of saturation.
